name: University of Veterinary Medicine Budapest
summary: Budapest veterinary university, teaching since 1787; English-taught veterinary medicine (5.5 years) and a five-year research zoology degree.

ib.text: No IB rule or exemption: everyone sits the entrance exam in biology, chemistry and English (written, then oral). Only transfers and French BCPST students can skip the written part.

programmes.name: Veterinary Medicine
programmes.about: Single-cycle veterinary degree in English, typically started straight after high school, ending in the DVM title after 5.5 years; the programme holds EAEVE accreditation.
programmes.ib: No IB rule or exemption: a written exam (50%) and an oral exam (50%) in biology, chemistry and English decide, and every applicant sits the oral exam.
programmes.selectionNote: Written exam in biology, chemistry and English; you need 50% overall (30% in biology and chemistry, 50% in English) to reach the oral exam, which covers motivation and science.

programmes.name: Research Zoology
programmes.about: Undivided ten-semester master's in English training zoological researchers, with individual research projects and scientific communication skills in the last two years.
programmes.ib: No IB rule is published: a written exam in biology, chemistry and English, then a 20-30 minute oral interview, decide.
programmes.selectionNote: Written exam (20 biology, 20 chemistry, 60 English questions) then an oral interview on motivation, background, biology and chemistry.

notes: Applications are rolling from January to 30 June, later if places remain; exams run online between March and July, with more rounds in August when there are vacancies.
One price is published for everyone, with no separate EU rate; you also pay a EUR 200 application fee and a EUR 250 exam fee, and a second exam attempt is free.
School-leavers get in only through the exam: the page names just transfers and the French BCPST year as exemptions from the written part, and says nothing about the IB.
